fullPassage: Think of the people who left Europe in the nineteenth century or Asia in the twentieth century to start a new life in the United States. At the outset of their journeys, few immigrants could have foretold exactly when and how they would achieve economic success in the new world, yet they set out for the "land of opportunity" nevertheless. More than that, many of them willingly accepted great hardship during the journey itself. The important point is that you have to take the leap without knowing the exact outcome in advance. A company that waits around for the numbers to "add up" will be left flat-footed in the race to the future. Without a clear-eyed view of the ultimate prize, a company is all too likely to abandon the race when unexpected hazards are encountered en route.
